A_target.statement:
Let $L$ be a [[Definition:Context-Free Language|context-free language]].
Then there exists $p \in \N$ such that every $w \in L$ with $\size w \ge p$ can be written $w = u v x y z$ with $\size {v y} \ge 1$, $\size {v x y} \le p$ and:
:$\forall i \ge 0: u v^i x y^i z \in L$

B_source.statement:
Let $L$ be a [[Definition:Regular Language|regular language]].
Then there exists $p \in \N$ such that every $w \in L$ with $\size w \ge p$ can be written $w = x y z$ with $\size y \ge 1$, $\size {x y} \le p$ and:
:$\forall i \ge 0: x y^i z \in L$

substitutions.the accepting path through a finite auto: a parse tree of the derivation
substitutions.a repeated state on that path: a repeated nonterminal on a root-to-leaf path of the tree
substitutions.the loop between the two occurrences: the subtree between the two occurrences of the nonterminal

derived.pumping the loop: substituting the outer subtree for the inner one, or vice versa, repeatedly
derived.one pumped segment: two pumped segments, since the repeated subtree contributes on both sides

object_map.reformulation: Replace the linear accepting path by a root-to-leaf path in a parse tree, so the repeated state becomes a repeated nonterminal.

validity_conditions: Both proofs are pigeonhole on a long structure: states along a path in the automaton case, nonterminals along a root-to-leaf path in the grammar case.
The tree has bounded branching, so a long word forces a long root-to-leaf path and hence a repeated nonterminal.
The conclusion necessarily has two pumped segments rather than one, because excising or duplicating a subtree affects the material on both sides of it.
proof_plan: Convert the grammar to [[Definition:Chomsky Normal Form|Chomsky normal form]], so parse trees are binary.

Let $m$ be the number of nonterminals and $p = 2^m$.
A parse tree of height $h$ yields at most $2^{h - 1}$ symbols, so $\size w \ge p$ forces a root-to-leaf path with more than $m$ nonterminals.
By the [[Pigeonhole Principle]], some nonterminal $A$ repeats on the lowest $m + 1$ nonterminals of that path.

Let the upper occurrence of $A$ yield $v x y$ and the lower yield $x$.
Replacing the lower subtree by the upper, or the upper by the lower, gives parse trees for $u v^i x y^i z$ for all $i \ge 0$.
Unlike the regular case, two segments $v$ and $y$ are pumped simultaneously.
{{qed}}
